notes: Robinhood Chain, chain id 4663. SOVRN.ONE (nine ASCII characters, one full stop) / SVO, 18 decimals, fixed 1,000,000,000 supply minted once to its deployer; plain ERC-20 with no owner, mint, tax, pause or blacklist. Pool: {IMD, SVO} ordered by address (IMD 0x5f7bb59365ce557c26dbcaa4ee9d39a4b95b7127, 18 decimals, is currency0 exactly when its address is lower than the token's); LP fee 12500 (1.25%), additional to hook fees; tick spacing 60. initialPrice is the launch's stated one-to-one value: the factory sets the real opening price, cap and currency order from its policy, and the hook accepts whatever it initializes. SovrnHook takes manager, token and factory in that flat order, no owner argument; its constructor checks only that manager and token have code, the token is not IMD and the factory is non-zero (no chain-id or IMD-code gate). Its six permissions encode 10444 (0x28cc); all others are false. Callbacks are PoolManager-only. Only the supplied factory may initialize its single pool; a second initialization and wrong keys are rejected. The constructor deploys the immutable LifeForceVault (vault()); no separate manifest entry. Every hook fee is paid in IMD: sells 3.5%; buys decay linearly from 50% at initialization to 3.5% at 3,600 s. Fees go directly to the vault when the manager's IMD covers the fee, else the hook mints one ERC-6909 claim counter (currency id uint160(IMD)) and anyone may redeemFees() to the vault. The vault derives reserves from its IMD balance: buyback floor(x*3000/10000), inference the rest; sync() checkpoints new IMD. Only REFUEL_SAFE 0xEb57c52272B90F989C41B739e2ccc5f00bF7697C may withdrawInference/withdrawBuyback, within the matching reserve, only to itself. Anyone may burn() the vault's whole SVO balance to DEAD. No owners, setters, minting, pause, blacklist or upgrade. For 60 minutes after initialization only the factory, or any sender while block.timestamp == openedAt, may add liquidity; removing is never blocked and pays no fee; afterwards anyone may add. A factory that seeds in a later block through a contract other than its $factory address is refused. PrepareLaunch mines the initcode for flags 10444: verified locally (predicted address and getHookPermissions both encode 10444; a local run of the admission floor with $poolManager, $token and $factory probes passed 11/11). forge test: 184 passed, 2 skipped (Fork4663.t.sol needs FORK_4663_RPC). Imported audit: both findings reproduced unchanged; the source was not changed in this step. (low) The opening exemption is keyed on the timestamp, not the block, so where several blocks share one second a non-factory sender can still add an IMD-only range beside the opening price in a later block of the opening second and have sellers fill it fee-free (both currency orders: 3.7457 IMD in, about 4.13M SVO out, the vault got only the 3.5% sell fee versus 50% on a direct buy at the same time); one second later the add reverts. (info) test/LiquidityLock.t.sol's 'IMD-only range' holds SVO only at the fixture price, so the suite does not exercise the parked route; a real IMD-only range there is 138240..156240 with IMD as currency0, or its mirror. External risks: IMD's single owner key (0x047F606fD5b2BaA5f5C6c4aB8958E45CB6B054B7) can enable a v4 transfer gate, blocklist and bridge; with the gate on and this pool unapproved, every IMD transfer into or out of the manager reverts, stopping buys, sells, redeemFees and IMD liquidity moves; IMD is a LayerZero OFT, so that key can in effect mint IMD. If IMD refuses the vault, direct fee takes revert. One key owns the real PoolManager and its protocol-fee controller (up to 0.1% of input per direction). Routers that sync(IMD) before the swap must add the buy fee. script/attest.py --check is the contributor's own record, not the verifier's attestation; it pins the previous manifest and already differs on the unchanged tree. No audit or security claim is made.
